raw_text:
This project is a research proposal on how and why to improve the Site Duty Process. For our efforts, we are focusing on one of our sites, Site 1. Through the root cause analysis, we found two main areas of delays: (1) inefficient process control; and (2) poor knowledge and skills of technicians. Given these findings, we will (1) collect data from Site 1 over three months, and use two requirements specification tests (RSTs) to determine the reasons of delays of each technician, and (2) send a one-year after-service survey to the enrolled technicians to observe their knowledge improvement and in-job skills.

- requirement specifications tests [RSTs]: we will take RSTs twice a a month, i.e. in the first two months and the last two months of our study. Each RST takes 15 minutes. It can be take place at each technician's workstation. The test consists of two parts: (a) technical skills check and (b) interpersonal skills check. The technician will make a series of decision, each of which discovers the technician's technical or interpersonal knowledge. Every answer is recorded as a success if the technician passes, or as a failure if the technician doesn't. As a result, we may know how many technicians can pass the RSTs on the two kinds of skills during those two periods, as from each category about the two kinds of requirements. In that way, we will discover which factors lead to the more processing delays in the two RSTs through the comparison of number of successes and number of failures between the involved technicians in each RST.
- on-the-job survey: at the end of the third months, we will conduct a one-year survey to the involved technicians from Site 1. By using the survey tool, we will evaluate their job performance and understanding degree on Site Duty Process Information System (SPIS), SCADA, Safety Alert, Incident History Card and Slope Gauge since the last year of their work. In that way, we will discover their change of learning and improvement of skills.

Data or evidence needed
